content: {"summary":"Both notification-worker pods experienced slow DNS lookups starting at 03:00 UTC on 23 July 2026, caused by the cluster default ndots:5 expanding short names into multiple queries, occasional lost UDP replies triggering 5‑second timeouts and retries, and rare double‑losses producing EAI_AGAIN errors; the issue lasted 215 minutes.","likely_cause":"Cluster default ndots:5 caused many DNS queries per short name, increasing the chance of lost replies that led to 5‑second timeout retries and occasional EAI_AGAIN failures.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The cluster default ndots:5 caused each short name to generate multiple DNS queries, increasing chance of lost replies.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"When a reply is missing, the resolver waits out its 5 s timeout and asks that query again"},{"text":"Lost DNS replies triggered a 5‑second timeout and retry, producing ~5 s lookup delays.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"When a reply is missing, the resolver waits out its 5 s timeout and asks that query again"},{"text":"When both attempts of a DNS query were lost, getaddrinfo returned EAI_AGAIN, causing rare failures.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#5"],"quote":"getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN needs both tries of one query lost (the default is attempts:2), which is rarer still"},{"text":"Notification‑worker deployments did not override ndots, so they inherited the cluster default and suffered the slowdown.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#0"],"quote":"The default belongs to the cluster; a Deployment has to override it to escape it"},{"text":"The slowdown persisted from 03:00 to 06:35 UTC on 23 July 2026, a total of 215 minutes.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#2"],"quote":"The incident record starts at 03:00 and ends at 06:35, which is 215 minutes"}],"next_checks":["Verify if ndots override is applied to notification-worker deployments","Monitor DNS reply loss rates and timeout occurrences","Check libuv thread‑pool utilization during bursts","Confirm no other services exhibit similar lookup delays"]}
